newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul students on hunger strike against crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Seoul students on hunger strike against crackdown.

text.p: Thirty-one militant South Korean students went on hunger strike on Thursday in protest against a government crackdown on a pro-Pyongyang campus body, witnesses said.
The students chained themselves to a steel rail along a ramp in the Roman Catholic cathedral in Seoul's Myongdong area. The cathedral is a traditional sanctuary for anti-government protesters.
"We have decided to stage an indefinite hunger strike because the government is using the death of two people as an excuse to suppress the student movement," their spokesman told Reuters.

The protesters are members of the Hanchongryon, which admitted responsibility for the torture killing of a suspected police spy last week. One policeman also was killed while trying to end a violent street demonstration by the group.
State prosecutors on Tuesday ordered the arrest of scores of Hanchongryon leaders and formally banned the group, which the government maintains takes orders from Pyongyang.
The militant group has called for the resignation of President Kim Young-sam and the reunification of the Korean peninsula under a formula suggested by communist North Korea.

"The Kim Young-sam regime is trying to avert a political crisis by cracking down on the Hanchongryon. It is trying to divert public attention from a scandal over the over-spending in the 1992 presidential elections," the spokesman said.
Opposition parties have alleged the president massively over-spent to get elected, and are demanding a full accounting.
Police have arrested three Hanchongryon activists over the fatal beating of Lee Suk, a factory worker, whose badly bruised body was delivered to a hospital last Wednesday.

Police said an autopsy showed Lee died as a result of the battering by students during a lengthy interrogation aimed at extracting a confession that he was a spy. His wrists had been tied with rope during the beating.
